title: Introduce cost-aware soft sampling and backpressure to tracing hotpath
creator: Asha Malik
description: We will introduce a cost-aware "soft sampling" mode and lightweight backpressure primitives on the tracer hotpath to reduce allocation and CPU overhead while preserving high-fidelity traces for expensive requests. The feature interposes a per-route, token-bucket-backed budget and a deferred metadata collection path so non-sampled requests pay only a tiny constant cost.
motivation: Recent profiling shows tracer allocations and lock contention account for ~18% of CPU in the ingress proxy under high QPS; emitted spans at peak traffic overload downstream collectors and inflate ingest cost. Existing prefilter approaches reduce volume but either add hotpath allocations or make hard decisions that increase missed tail traces. We need a middle ground that is adaptive to workload cost and retains tail fidelity.
design_decisions:
- Soft sampling: always create a lightweight TraceID and attach a 1-byte sampling hint on the hotpath; expensive metadata (full span objects, stack traces, annotations) are collected only if later sampling decision permits emission.
- Cost budget: per-route token bucket tracks an approximate "trace-cost" budget in units proportional to expected emitted bytes. Buckets are refilled by route-configured rates.
- Stochastic uplift at tail: a late-bound tail detector (latency/error heuristic) can override bucket denial to force retention for slow/errorful requests.
- Backpressure: when global emission rate exceeds backpressure threshold, we mark low-priority routes to drop full-emission even if their bucket allows it; this is implemented via an atomic flag read in hotpath.
- Low-alloc paths: use preallocated small TraceHeader structs and arena allocations for deferred metadata to avoid per-request heap allocs.
- Signals: maintain realtime counters (bucket fill, dropped_by_backpressure, uplifted_by_tail) for telemetry and autoscaling signals.
implementation_plan: 1) Add lightweight TraceHeader struct and hotpath API that writes only TraceID + sampling_hint (C++/Go variants). 2) Implement per-route token-bucket store in ingress with O(1) read on hotpath. 3) Implement deferred metadata buffer (arena) attached to request context, populated only when sampling is granted. 4) Implement tail detector hook: simple latency threshold + recent-error-rate spike detector that can request uplift. 5) Add global backpressure manager (configurable thresholds) that sets route-level allowlist/deny flags. 6) Add feature flag + config to enable soft-sampling per deployment. 7) Bench and iterate on allocations and lock-free properties.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token-bucket correctness and refill logic.
- Microbenchmarks comparing allocations, latency, and throughput with and without soft-sampling. Goal: reduce tracer allocations on hotpath by >=40% and CPU by >=20% at 95th QPS.
- Integration tests: end-to-end trace emission correctness when uplift occurs; ensure no metadata loss for uplifted traces.
- Chaos: simulate bursts that trigger backpressure and verify low-priority routes get denied emission and metrics reflect counts.
- Observability: create dashboards for dropped_by_backpressure, uplifted_by_tail, per-route emitted_spans/s, and tracer_cpu_pct.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable on a single non-critical service at 10% traffic for 48h. Monitor metrics and SLOs. Phase 2: expand to staging and additional services with increased token rates. Phase 3: global opt-in behind runtime-1.22 with default off; enable for performance tier customers. Immediate rollback via feature flag if emitted span rate falls below threshold or if tail-P99 latency regression > 1ms.
metrics_and_slo:
- Hotpath tracer allocations (bytes / request) target: -40% vs baseline.
- Tracer CPU% goal: -20% at 95th percentile QPS.
- Emitted spans per second: expected -50% on high-cardinality routes.
- Tail preservation: uplifted trace capture rate >= 95% for requests > 95th latency percentile.
- No user-facing error increase attributable to tracer changes.
progress_notes:
2026-03-01: Ticket created by Asha after spike incident post-release.
2026-03-03: Spike reproducer and profiler flamegraph attached to Confluence. Found contention primarily in span encoder and mutex around global counters.
2026-03-05: Prototype lightweight TraceHeader implemented (branch: tracing/soft-sample-proto). Microbenchmarks show 28% alloc reduction.
2026-03-07: Design review with PM and Observability: agreed to token-bucket per-route and tail-uplift strategy; request to add per-tenant override. Action: Connor to update PR.
2026-03-09: Bench improvements by switching arena to slab allocator reduced allocs further; extended benchmark shows 42% allocation reduction and ~18% CPU reduction at target load.
2026-03-10: Started integration tests; discovered race in bucket refill when config reloads — mitigation: hold RCU-style reader lock during reload (low-cost). Planning canary on 2026-03-15.
notes:
- Avoid adding any new heap allocations on the non-sampled path; even temporarybox allocations accumulate under load.
- Keep sampling_hint compact to allow downstream systems to rehydrate traces if needed.
- We may follow-up with a telemetry pump that periodically pushes sampled metadata for sampled traces to reduce tail collector pressure.
- Consider a future enhancement that credits token budgets for traces where downstream telemetry shows high business value.
acceptance_criteria:
- Soft sampling compiled and feature-flagged in runtime-1.22.
- Hotpath allocations reduced >=40% in microbench.
- Tail uplift mechanism successfully captures >=95% of 95th+ latency requests in integration tests.
- Dashboards and alerts instrumented and validated during canary.
- No increase in customer-facing errors attributable to this change during canary.
review_feedback:
- PM (Ravi Patel): ensure per-tenant overrides for enterprise customers.
- Security (Lena Ortiz): confirm TraceID entropy unchanged and that sampling hints do not leak PII.
- Performance (Marta Nguyen): suggested avoiding atomic ops for every request; use sharded counters.
- Action items: add privacy checklist and run PR through security gating.
final_comments: This approach balances cost reduction with tail fidelity by making the hotpath as cheap as possible while allowing a late decision for important requests. If successful, this will be a building block for more aggressive emission controls (e.g., probabilistic payload truncation).
